title: One widen per step, every board valid
short: Basket = 21 + one witness per prime. Each step widens one point into a basket block; every board along the way must be a valid witness.
long: Start from the 1×1 board. A step replaces one point by a block from the basket. Every board produced must use each diagonal at most once. After all boards of size n are built, every valid arrangement of size n with no built witness is a prime; its dictionary-first witness joins the basket.

title: One widen per step, every board valid, primes add all witnesses
short: As above, but each prime puts all of its witnesses in the basket.
long: Same as the first experiment, except that a prime contributes every one of its witnesses to the basket, not just one.

title: Composite blocks in the basket
short: Every witness built so far joins the basket, not just primes.
long: Every valid witness found at size n (built or prime) becomes a basket block. Widening one point into a composite block such as 321 is the same as several widens at once, so this lets the search pass through invalid boards.

title: Invalid boards allowed in between
short: Boards along the way may repeat a diagonal; only the final board must be valid. One witness per prime.
long: Same steps, but intermediate boards may repeat diagonals; an arrangement counts as built if some valid board of that size was produced. Primes contribute one witness.

title: Invalid boards allowed, primes add all witnesses
short: As above, with every witness of each prime in the basket.
long: As the previous experiment, with all witnesses of each prime added.

title: Invalid boards allowed, plus the 12 frame
short: Adds 12 (two points on the main diagonal) to the basket so corner gluing (direct sums) is possible.
long: 12 repeats diagonal 0, so it is never a witness and was never in the basket; without it no direct sum can be built. Here it is added as a frame-only block. One witness per prime.

title: Invalid boards allowed, 12 frame, primes add all witnesses
long: Invalid intermediates, 12 in the basket, every witness of each prime added.

title: Robust expansion
short: Does D have a smaller arrangement D′ with marked stones such that every witness of D′ expands to a witness of D?
long: Blocks 21, 132, 213, 321. For each smaller arrangement D′ and choice of marked stones, expand every witness of D′. Robust: all of them give witnesses of the same D. Listed: arrangements (no tight cut, up to mirror) with no robust expansion.

title: Smallest frame set (greedy)
short: Which block-free outer permutations (frames) are needed so every arrangement except P_n is some frame with blocks filled in? n ≤ 9.
long: Every permutation is uniquely a frame with blocks filled in (frames 12/21 for corner gluing). For every no-tight-cut arrangement except P_n with n ≤ 9, collect the frames of its witnesses, then pick frames greedily (most arrangements covered first) until all are covered. Grouped by frame size; 'covers' = arrangements newly covered when picked. Frames that repeat a diagonal are marked.

title: Recursive build from the frame set
short: Using only the frame set (plus 12, 21) at every level, which arrangements get built?
long: A witness is buildable if its frame is in the set (or 12/21) and each of its blocks is buildable, recursively. An arrangement is reached if some witness is buildable. Listed: arrangements (no tight cut, up to mirror) not reached. Block counts are over witnesses whose top frame is in the set.
